references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the cities will be destroyed and lie desolate, reflecting the judgment in Leviticus that cities should be laid in ruins.
Isaiah describes how the sanctuary has been burned up and lies in ruins, fulfilling the threat that God would destroy the sanctuaries.
Jeremiah prophesies that Zion shall be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become heaps of rubble, including the temple mount.
Lamentations describes how the Lord has rejected His altar and forsaken His sanctuary, fulfilling the judgment in Leviticus.
Ezekiel prophesies that God will profane His sanctuary, reflecting the threat to destroy the sanctuaries.
Amos conveys that God hates and rejects the festivals and will not smell the fragrance of the sacrifices, directly echoing 'I will not smell your pleasing aroma' in Leviticus.
Micah prophesies that Zion shall be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become heaps of rubble, including the temple mount.
The continuation of the same judgment in Leviticus where the land shall lie desolate and cities remain in ruins.
Moses warns in Deuteronomy that enemies will besiege the cities until they fall, as part of the consequences of breaking the covenant.
Historical fulfillment of the judgment when the Babylonians burned the house of the Lord, the king's house, and all the houses in Jerusalem.
